Relever du sens contraire à celui dont ils sont naturellement couchés, en parlant des cheveux et du poil.

examples.text: Rebrousser les cheveux. — Rebrousser le poil d’un chat.
Il se teignait la moustache, qu’il portait toute raide et rebroussée.

glosses: Retourner subitement en arrière.

examples.text: […] les conseillers féroces de Louis XVI font rebrousser des farines que le commerce apporte dans Paris fidèle et affamé.
Comme il allait à la campagne, il reçut une nouvelle qui le fit rebrousser aussitôt.
— Les rivières rebrousseront contre leur source, vers leur source, avant que… Elles remonteront vers leur source, avant que…

glosses: Se redresser.

examples.text:
— Mes bien chers frères…
L’auditoire, un peu couché, se rebroussa.

glosses: To show up; to appear suddenly or unexpectedly.

examples.text: Is this your t-shirt that turned up in my drawer?
I don't like people turning up without an appointment.

Highly providential was the appearance on the scene of Corny Kelleher when Stephen was blissfully unconscious but for that man in the gap turning up at the eleventh hour the finis might have been that he might have been a candidate for the accident ward […]
I haven't booked, so I don't have a clue as to whether the service will be busy or not. Supposedly, reservations are compulsory, but I want to find out what would happen if you just turn up.

glosses: To cause to appear; to find by searching, etc.

examples.text: I spent hours in the archives, but couldn't turn up anything on the alleged criminal.

glosses: To increase the amount of something by means of a control, such as the volume, heat, or light.

examples.text: Turn up the radio and sing along.

Turn the rhythm up, don't you wanna just
Come along for the ride?

glosses: To reposition by rotating, flipping, etc., upwards.

examples.text: He turned up his collar against the cold.

glosses: To belay or make fast (a line on a cleat or pin).

examples.text: Turn up the main halyard.

glosses: To party hard, especially when involving alcohol or drugs.

examples.text: We're going to turn up at the concert tonight.

glosses: To acquit.

examples.text: Thirty-six were cast for death, and only one was ‘topped’ (hanged), the very one that expected to be ‘turned up’ (acquitted) for highway robbery.

glosses: Alternative spelling of turn-up.
To reverse direction and retrace one's steps.

examples.text: Realising he had forgotten his briefcase, he turned back and re-entered the office.

Turning back, then, toward the basement staircase, she began to grope her way through blinding darkness, but had taken only a few uncertain steps when, of a sudden, she stopped short and for a little stood like a stricken thing, quite motionless save that she quaked to her very marrow in the grasp of a great and enervating fear.

glosses: To cause to reverse direction and retrace one's steps.

examples.text: The barrage of machine-gun fire turned back the encroaching soldiers.

Pilton Yard, the Lynton & Barnstaple headquarters, has been taken over by a fur trading firm, and would-be trespassers to the old engine-shed are turned back by the pungent odour of heaps of carcases.

glosses: To return to a previous state of being.

examples.text: He stopped drinking for a couple of years, but now he has turned back to his old ways.
Once we take this decision, there's no turning back.

Welcome to your life
There's no turning back
Even while we sleep
We will find you

glosses: To prevent, or refuse to allow, passage or progress.

examples.text: The soldiers turned back all the refugees at the frontier.

glosses: To adjust to a previous setting.

examples.text: In Autumn we normally turn the clocks back one hour.
I love that song: turn back to it!

glosses: To fold something back; to fold down.

examples.text: When you make the bed, please always turn the sheet back over the blanket.

glosses: To give back; to return.

examples.text:
We turn not back the silks upon the merchants,
When we have soiled them; nor the remainder viands.
